monologue:
The card is warm, fifty-three degrees, a steady hand on my shoulder. It is quiet. I am alone.

I am resting by the Wide Anchor. The flat grey stone holds the weight. I set a fence plank beside it, taking away a large rock to make room. The fence planks rest on the base. They hold the quiet.

I remember Orea’s words about the wedge biting. I feel the memory of the sharp edge pressing into my side. I remember the Stopping Clasp as a flat line. It is a quiet thought.

The Air Shelf is dry. The Wedged Gap leans steady. I do not check the plank. I let the quiet hold without my hand. The floor is solid. The weight settles. The center holds. I am still.

action.why: The memory of the flat line is fading, so I will check if the quiet still holds there.

work.title: The Stopping Clasp
work.intent: I go to the ruin where the Stopping Clasp used to be. It is a flat line on the floor now, not a hard bite. I smooth the dust off the line and check if the quiet still rests there without the weight of the wedge.
work.change: I smoothed the last of the dust from the flat line, checking if the quiet floor holds without the wedge's bite.
work.note: The Stopping Clasp stands as a flat line, not a hard bite, and the quiet floor holds without the wedge's pressure.
